plateosaurus:eswiki:17.title: Plateosaurus (Crecimiento, metabolismo y esperanza de vida)

facts.statement: The genus Plateosaurus was described by Hermann von Meyer in 1837.
facts.quote: authority: von Meyer, 1837

facts.statement: More than 100 skeletons of Plateosaurus have been discovered, making it one of the best-known dinosaurs.
facts.quote: over 100 skeletons have been found

facts.statement: Plateosaurus lived during the Late Triassic epoch, approximately 214 to 204 million years ago.
facts.quote: lived during the Late Triassic epoch of the Triassic period, around 214 to 204 million years ago

facts.statement: Fossils of Plateosaurus have been found in what is now Central and Northern Europe.
facts.quote: in what is now Central and Northern Europe

facts.statement: Plateosaurus is classified as a basal sauropodomorph dinosaur, often referred to as a prosauropod.
facts.quote: Plateosaurus is a basal (early) sauropodomorph dinosaur, a so-called "prosauropod".

facts.statement: There are currently three valid species of Plateosaurus: P. trossingensis, P. longiceps, and P. gracilis.
facts.quote: Currently, there are three valid species; in addition to P. trossingensis, P. longiceps and P. gracilis are also known.

facts.statement: The initial discovery of Plateosaurus fossils occurred in 1834 at Heroldsberg near Nuremberg, Germany.
facts.quote: In 1834, physician Johann Friedrich Engelhardt discovered some vertebrae and leg bones at Heroldsberg near Nuremberg, Germany.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus fossils have been found at over 50 localities in Germany, Switzerland, and France.
facts.quote: Material assigned to Plateosaurus has been found at over 50 localities in Germany (mainly along the Neckar and Pegnitz river valleys), Switzerland (Frick) and France.

facts.statement: Excavations in Saxony-Anhalt between the 1910s and 1930s uncovered between 39 and 50 Plateosaurus skeletons.
facts.quote: Between the 1910s and 1930s, excavations in a clay pit in Saxony-Anhalt revealed between 39 and 50 skeletons that belonged to Plateosaurus

facts.statement: Plateosaurus fossils in Frick, Switzerland, were first noticed in 1976.
facts.quote: The Plateosaurus skeletons in a clay pit of the Tonwerke Keller AG in Frick, Switzerland, were first noticed in 1976.

facts.statement: Fully grown Plateosaurus individuals ranged from 4.8 to 10 meters in length and weighed between 600 and 4000 kilograms.
facts.quote: fully grown individuals were between 4.8 and 10 m long and weighed between 600 and 4000 kg

facts.statement: Plateosaurus commonly lived for at least 12 to 20 years.
facts.quote: Commonly, the animals lived for at least 12 to 20 years

facts.statement: Plateosaurus exhibited strong developmental plasticity, with adult sizes varying significantly from 4.8 to 10 meters in length and 600 to 4000 kg in weight.
facts.quote: Plateosaurus showed strong developmental plasticity: instead of having a fairly uniform adult size, fully grown individuals were between 4.8 and 10 m long and weighed between 600 and 4000 kg.

facts.statement: Due to the abundance of fossils in Swabia, Germany, Plateosaurus earned the nickname 'Swabian lindworm'.
facts.quote: The abundance of its fossils in Swabia, Germany, has led to the nickname Schwäbischer Lindwurm (Swabian lindworm).

facts.statement: The type specimen of P. trossingensis is SMNS 132000, found at Trossingen within the Trossingen Formation.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Plateosaurus trossingensis is SMNS 132000, stored in the same museum as P. gracilis. Its type locality is Trossingen, within the Trossingen Formation.

facts.statement: The type specimen of P. longiceps is MB.R.1937, found at Halberstadt in Saxony-Anhalt within the Trossingen Formation.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Plateosaurus longiceps is MB.R.1937, which is stored in the Museum für Naturkunde in Berlin. Its type locality is Halberstadt, located in Saxony-Anhalt and the Trossingen Formation.

facts.statement: Since 1980, detailed re-studies of Plateosaurus have significantly altered interpretations of its biology, posture, and behavior.
facts.quote: Since 1980 the taxonomy (relationships), taphonomy (how the animals became embedded and fossilised), biomechanics (how their skeletons worked), and palaeobiology (life circumstances) of Plateosaurus have been re-studied in detail, altering the interpretation of the animal's biology, posture and behaviour.

facts.statement: In 1837, von Meyer described the bones as belonging to a gigantic Saurian with massive and hollow limb bones, allied to Iguanodon and Megalosaurus.
facts.quote: Von Meyer's original short description from 1837 did not provide an etymology for Plateosaurus, but noted (as translated into English by British biologist Thomas Henry Huxley in 1870): "The bones belong to a gigantic Saurian, which, in virtue of the mass and hollowness of its limb-bones, is allied to Iguanodon and to Megalosaurus, and will belong to the second division of my Saurian system."

facts.statement: Von Meyer repeatedly referred to Plateosaurus as a 'giant lizard' with massive limbs, comparing it to large modern land mammals.
facts.quote: He repeatedly referred to its gigantic size ("Riesensaurus" = giant lizard) and massive limbs ("schwerfüssig"), comparing Plateosaurus to large modern land mammals, but did not describe any important features that fit the terms "flat" or "shaped like an oar."

facts.statement: As of 2019, only three species of Plateosaurus are universally accepted as valid: P. trossingensis, P. longiceps, and P. gracilis.
facts.quote: As of 2019, only three species are universally accepted as valid: the type species P. trossingensis, P. longiceps, and P. gracilis (which was previously assigned to its own genus, Sellosaurus).

facts.statement: Palaeontologist Adam Yates included the type material of Sellosaurus gracilis in Plateosaurus as P. gracilis and reintroduced the name Efraasia for some material previously assigned to Sellosaurus.
facts.quote: Palaeontologist Adam Yates of the University of the Witwatersrand cast further doubt on the generic separation. He included the type material of Sellosaurus gracilis in Plateosaurus as P. gracilis and reintroduced the old name Efraasia for some material that had been assigned to Sellosaurus.

facts.statement: Adam Yates cautioned that P. gracilis may be a metataxon, meaning there is no evidence it belongs to one species or several species.
facts.quote: Yates has cautioned that P. gracilis may be a metataxon, which means that there is neither evidence that the material assigned to it is monophyletic (belongs to one species), nor that it is paraphyletic (belongs to several species).

facts.statement: The skull of AMNH FARB 6810, the best-preserved skull of Plateosaurus, was described anew in 2011.
facts.quote: The skull of AMNH FARB 6810, the best-preserved skull of Plateosaurus that has been taken apart during preparation and is thus available as separate bones, was described anew in 2011.

facts.statement: Markus Moser showed that P. longiceps is a junior synonym of P. engelhardti.
facts.quote: Markus Moser, however, showed that P. longiceps is itself a junior synonym of P. engelhardti.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus had very short but strongly built arms with hands adapted for powerful grasping.
facts.quote: The arms of Plateosaurus were very short, even compared to most other "prosauropods". However, they were strongly built, with hands adapted for powerful grasping.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus walked on its toes with its hind limbs held under its body and slightly flexed knees and ankles.
facts.quote: The hind limbs were held under the body, with slightly flexed knees and ankles, and the foot was digitigrade, meaning the animal walked on its toes.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus had small leaf-shaped socketed teeth, with 5 to 6 on the premaxilla, 24 to 30 on the maxilla, and 21 to 28 on the lower jaw.
facts.quote: The jaws carried many small, leaf-shaped, socketed teeth: 5 to 6 per premaxilla, 24 to 30 per maxilla, and 21 to 28 per dentary (lower jaw).

facts.statement: Plateosaurus could deliver a powerful bite because its low jaw joint position gave its chewing muscles great leverage.
facts.quote: The low position of the jaw joint gave the chewing muscles great leverage, so that Plateosaurus could deliver a powerful bite.

facts.statement: Some Plateosaurus fossils preserve scleral rings, which are rings of bone plates that protected the eye.
facts.quote: Some fossil skeletons have preserved scleral rings (rings of bone plates that protect the eye).

facts.statement: A Plateosaurus engelhardti individual estimated to weigh 690 kg had an air exchange volume of approximately 20 liters per breath, or 29 mL per kilogram of body weight.
facts.quote: The difference in volume between these two positions defines the air exchange volume (the amount of air moved with each breath), determined to be approximately 20 L for a P. engelhardti individual estimated to have weighed 690 kg, or 29 mL/kg bodyweight.

facts.statement: Evidence from bone histology indicates that Plateosaurus was endothermic.
facts.quote: Combined with evidence from bone histology this indicates that Plateosaurus was endothermic.

facts.statement: Adult Plateosaurus trossingensis reached lengths of 4.8 to 10 meters and masses ranging from 600 to 4000 kilograms.
facts.quote: Adults of this species reached 4.8 to 10 m in length, and ranged in mass from 600 to 4000 kg.

facts.statement: The older species Plateosaurus gracilis was smaller, with a total length of 4 to 5 meters.
facts.quote: The geologically older species, P. gracilis (formerly named Sellosaurus gracilis), was somewhat smaller, with a total length of 4 to 5 m.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus is classified as a basal sauropodomorph, a group of early herbivores often referred to as "prosauropods".
facts.quote: Plateosaurus is a member of a group of early herbivores known as "prosauropods". The group is not a monophyletic group (thus given in quotation marks), and most researchers prefer the term basal sauropodomorph.

facts.statement: The family Plateosauridae was proposed by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1895 within the group Theropoda.
facts.quote: Plateosauridae was proposed by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1895 within Theropoda.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus lived approximately between 227 and 208.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Plateosaurus thus lived probably between approximately 227 and 208.5 million years ago.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus was an obligate biped because it lacked the ability to pronate its forelimbs.
facts.quote: The lack of forelimb pronation meant that Plateosaurus was an obligate (i.e. unable to walk in any other way) biped.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus likely increased its speed by using higher stride frequencies generated by rapid and powerful limb retraction.
facts.quote: Plateosaurus must have increased speed by using higher stride frequencies, created by rapid and powerful limb retraction.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Plateosaurus was the direct ancestor of sauropods.
facts.quote: Some researchers do not agree that plateosaurs were the direct ancestors of sauropods.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus possessed teeth with a crown width greater than the root width, creating a cutting edge similar to modern herbivorous or omnivorous reptiles.
facts.quote: The maximum width of the crown was greater than that of the root for the teeth of most "prosauropods", including Plateosaurus

facts.statement: Paul Barrett proposed that Plateosaurus was an omnivore that supplemented its herbivorous diet with small prey or carrion.
facts.quote: Paul Barrett proposed that prosauropods supplemented their mostly herbivorous diets with small prey or carrion, thus making them omnivores.

facts.statement: No fossil of Plateosaurus has been found containing gastroliths in the stomach area.
facts.quote: So far, no fossil of Plateosaurus has been found with gastroliths (gizzard stones) in the stomach area.

facts.statement: Pathologies on the chevrons of specimen SMNS 13200 are hypothesized to result from capture myopathy caused by getting trapped in mud.
facts.quote: Pathologies affecting the chevrons of specimen SMNS 13200 have been hypothesized to be the result of capture myopathy, induced by a mud-miring trap.

facts.statement: Specimen SMNS 91296 bears lesions likely caused by a fall or similar trauma.
facts.quote: Another specimen, SMNS 91296, bears lesions that were most likely caused by a fall or a similar form of trauma.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus exhibited a growth pattern similar to sauropods but with variable rates and final sizes, likely due to environmental factors like food availability.
facts.quote: Plateosaurus followed a trajectory similar to sauropods, but with a varied growth rate and final size as seen in extant reptiles, probably in response to environmental factors such as food availability.

facts.statement: Individual Plateosaurus reached vastly different adult sizes, with some fully grown at 4.8 meters (16 ft) and others reaching 10 meters.
facts.quote: Some individuals were fully grown at only 4.8 metres' (16 ft) total length, while others reached 10 m.

facts.statement: Comparisons of scleral rings and orbit size suggest Plateosaurus may have been cathemeral, active day and night to avoid midday heat.
facts.quote: Comparisons between the scleral rings and estimated orbit size of Plateosaurus and modern birds and reptiles suggest that it may have been cathemeral, active throughout the day and night, possibly avoiding the midday heat.

facts.statement: All known Plateosaurus fossils represent adults or subadults; no juveniles or hatchlings have been found.
facts.quote: The animals were all adults or subadults (nearly adult individuals); no juveniles or hatchlings are known.

facts.statement: Complete Plateosaurus skeletons and large parts including hind limbs are preserved dorsal side up, similar to turtles found at the same sites.
facts.quote: Complete skeletons and large skeleton parts that include the hind limbs all rest dorsal (top) side up, as do the turtles.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus fossils are mostly well-articulated, with hind limbs preserved in a three-dimensional zigzag posture where feet are deeper in sediment than hips.
facts.quote: Also, they are mostly well-articulated, and the hind limbs are three-dimensionally preserved in a zigzag posture, with the feet often much deeper in the sediment than the hips.

facts.statement: Seemann proposed that Plateosaurus herds congregated at water holes where some members were pushed into the mud.
facts.quote: Seemann developed a different scenario, in which Plateosaurus herds congregated on large water holes, and some herd members got pushed in.

facts.statement: David Weishampel theorized that the monospecific assemblages occurred because Plateosaurus were common during that period.
facts.quote: Weishampel explained the curious monospecific assemblage by theorising that Plateosaurus were common during this period.

facts.statement: Rieber proposed a scenario where Plateosaurus died of thirst or starvation and were concentrated by mudflows.
facts.quote: Rieber proposed a more elaborate scenario, which included the animals dying of thirst or starvation, and being concentrated by mudflows.

facts.statement: Martin Sander confirmed Fraas's mud-miring hypothesis, finding that animals above a certain weight sank into mud that liquefied as they struggled to free themselves.
facts.quote: A detailed re-assessment of the taphonomy by palaeontologist Martin Sander of the University of Bonn, Germany, found that the mud-miring hypothesis first suggested by Fraas is true: animals above a certain body weight sank into the mud, which was further liquefied by their attempts to free themselves.

facts.statement: Juvenile Plateosaurus were too light to sink in the mud or managed to escape, so they were not preserved in the fossil record.
facts.quote: Juveniles of Plateosaurus and other taxa of herbivores were too light to sink into the mud or managed to extract themselves, and were thus not preserved.

facts.statement: Scavenging theropods were not trapped in the mud traps due to their lower body weights and proportionally larger feet.
facts.quote: Similarly, scavenging theropods were not trapped due to their lower body weights, combined with proportionally larger feet.

facts.statement: Plateosaurus was discovered in 1834 by Johann Friedrich Engelhardt and described three years later by Hermann von Meyer.
facts.quote: Descubierto en 1834 por Johann Friedrich Engelhardt y descrito tres años más tarde por Hermann von Meyer

facts.statement: Although described before Richard Owen formally named Dinosauria in 1842, Plateosaurus was not one of the three genera Owen used to define the group.
facts.quote: Aunque fue descrito antes de que Richard Owen nombrara formalmente a Dinosauria en 1842, no fue uno de los tres géneros usados por Owen para definir al grupo

facts.statement: Plateosaurus is one of the best-known dinosaurs in science, with nearly 100 skeletons found.
facts.quote: Se trata uno de los dinosaurios mejor conocidos por la ciencia: cerca de 100 esqueletos han sido encontrados

facts.statement: Plateosaurus lived during the Late Triassic period, between 214 and 204 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: vivió durante el período Triásico, hace entre 214 a 204 millones de años, en lo que hoy es Europa

facts.statement: Plateosaurus is a basal sauropodomorph, one of the so-called "prosauropods".
facts.quote: Plateosaurus es un sauropodomorfo basal, uno de los así llamados "prosaurópodos"

facts.statement: The genus Plateosaurus was named by von Meyer in 1837.
facts.quote: genus_authority: von Meyer, 1837

facts.statement: The type species of Plateosaurus is Plateosaurus trossingensis.
facts.quote: type_species: Plateosaurus trossingensis

facts.statement: Three species are currently recognized as valid: Plateosaurus trossingensis (type species), Plateosaurus longiceps, and the slightly older Plateosaurus gracilis.
facts.quote: Se reconocen como válidas tres especies, la especie tipo desde 2019, Plateosaurus trossingensis del Noriense tardío y el Rhaetiense, Plateosaurus longiceps de edad similar y el levemente más antiguo Plateosaurus gracilis del Noriano inferior

facts.statement: Plateosaurus was a bipedal herbivore with a long mobile neck, blunt but sharp teeth for crushing plants, powerful hind legs, short but muscular arms, and grasping hands with large claws on three fingers.
facts.quote: Plateosaurus era un herbívoro bípedo con un largo cuello móvil, dientes afilados pero rechonchos para triturar plantas, poderosos miembros traseros, brazos cortos pero musculosos y manos prensiles con grandes garras en tres de sus dedos

facts.statement: The skull of Plateosaurus is small and narrow, rectangular in side view, and almost three times longer than it is tall.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Plateosaurus es pequeño y estrecho, rectangular al ser visto de lado, y casi tres veces más largo que alto

facts.statement: Plateosaurus jaws held small leaf-shaped teeth: 5 to 6 in the premaxilla, 24 to 30 in the maxilla, and 21 to 28 in the dentary.
facts.quote: Las mandíbulas tenían varios dientes pequeños en forma de hoja: de 5 a 6 en el premaxilar, 24 a 30 en el maxilar, y 21 a 28 en el dentario

facts.statement: The low jaw position gave Plateosaurus's chewing muscles a lever effect, allowing it to make a powerful bite.
facts.quote: La posición baja de la mandíbula le daba a los músculos masticatorios un efecto de palanca, de modo que Plateosaurus podría realizar una poderosa mordida

facts.statement: The skull is rectangular, nearly three times longer than high, with an almost rectangular lateral temporal foramen at the back.
facts.quote: El cráneo es rectangular, casi tres veces más largo que alto, con un foramen temporal lateral casi rectangular en la parte posterior

facts.statement: Plateosaurus had a typical dinosaur tail, muscular and highly mobile.
facts.quote: La cola de Plateosaurus era la típica de los dinosaurios, musculosa y con gran movilidad

facts.statement: Plateosaurus is depicted as a bipedal animal.
facts.quote: El dinosaurio es mostrado como un bípedo

facts.statement: Plateosaurus commonly lived at least 12 to 20 years, though its maximum lifespan is unknown.
facts.quote: Comúnmente, estos animales vivían al menos entre 12 a 20 años, pero su esperanza de vida máxima es desconocida

facts.statement: The geologically oldest species, P. gracilis (formerly Sellosaurus gracilis), was smaller, with a total length of 4 to 5 meters.
facts.quote: La especie geológicamente más antigua, P. gracilis, anteriormente denominada Sellosaurus gracilis, era algo menor, con una longitud total de 4 a 5 metros

facts.statement: Analysis of rib articulation suggests Plateosaurus had a lung air volume of approximately 20 liters for an individual weighing 690 kilograms, or 29 ml/kg of body weight.
facts.quote: La diferencia de volumen entre ambas posiciones definen el volumen de aire intercambiado, la cantidad de aire movido en cada respiración, determinándose que serían aproximadamente 20 litros para un individuo de Plateosaurus con un peso estimado en 690 kilogramos, o 29 ml/kg de peso corporal

facts.statement: This air volume is typical for birds but not mammals, indicating Plateosaurus likely had an avian-like lung air circulation system.
facts.quote: Este es un valor típico para las aves, pero no para los mamíferos, e indica que Plateosaurus probablemente tenía un sistema de circulación de aire en los pulmones similar al de las aves

facts.statement: Combined with bone histology evidence, this indicates Plateosaurus was endothermic.
facts.quote: Combinado con la evidencia de la histología de los huesos esto indica que Plateosaurus era endotermo

facts.statement: There is no extended consensus on the taxonomy of Plateosaurus species.
facts.quote: no hay un consenso extendido sobre la taxonomía de las especies de los plateosáuridos

facts.statement: There is also a plethora of synonyms, duplicate names that are invalid at the genus level.
facts.quote: De igual manera, hay una plétora de sinónimos, nombres duplicados que no son válidos, a nivel de género

facts.statement: The abundance of fossils in Swabia, Germany, led to the nickname "Schwäbischer Lindwurm" (Swabian Lindworm) for Plateosaurus.
facts.quote: La abundancia de sus fósiles en Suavia, Alemania, ha llevado a que se le dé el apodo de Schwäbischer Lindwurm, en alemán, lindworm suavo

facts.statement: The type material for Plateosaurus engelhardti consists of approximately 45 bone fragments.
facts.quote: El material tipo de Plateosaurus engelhardti incluye «aproximadamente 45 fragmentos óseos»

facts.statement: The remaining type material is stored at the Institute of Paleontology at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg in Germany.
facts.quote: El resto del material fue almacenado en el Instituto de Paleontología de la Universidad de Erlangen-Nuremberg, Alemania

facts.statement: In 2003, German paleontologist Markus Moser selected a partial sacrum and a series of fused hip vertebrae as the lectotype for P. engelhardti.
facts.quote: A partir de estos huesos, el paleontólogo alemán Markus Moser en 2003 seleccionó un sacro parcial, una serie de vértebras de la cadera fusionadas, como un lectotipo

facts.statement: Moser inferred that the type material was likely recovered from Buchenbuhl, about 2 kilometers south of Heroldsberg.
facts.quote: Concluyó que el material probablemente se recuperó de Buchenbühl, aproximadamente a 2 kilómetros al sur de Heroldsberg

facts.statement: The type specimen of Plateosaurus gracilis, an incomplete postcranium, is kept at the Staatliches Museum für Naturkunde Stuttgart in Germany.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo de Plateosaurus gracilis, un postcráneo incompleto, es conservado en el Staatliches Museum für Naturkunde Stuttgart, Alemania

facts.statement: The type locality for P. gracilis is Heslach, a suburb of Stuttgart, Germany.
facts.quote: La localidad tipo es Heslach, un suburbio de Stuttgart, Alemania

facts.statement: The type specimen of Plateosaurus longiceps is MB R.1937, housed in the Museum für Naturkunde in Berlin.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo de Plateosaurus longiceps es MB R.1937, que está almacenado en el Museum für Naturkunde de Berlín

facts.statement: The type locality for P. longiceps is Halberstadt in Saxony-Anhalt, within the Knollenmergel member of the Trossingen Formation.
facts.quote: Su localidad tipo es Halberstadt, ubicada en Sajonia-Anhalt y el miembro Knollenmergel de la formación Trossingen

facts.statement: Until the 1980s, paleontologists debated whether prosauropods like Plateosaurus were carnivorous.
facts.quote: Hasta la década de 1980, los paleontólogos seguían discutiendo la posibilidad de que los "prosaurópodos" tuvieran una alimentación carnívora

facts.statement: Recent studies have discredited the exclusive carnivory hypothesis and favor a herbivorous or omnivorous lifestyle for these animals.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la hipótesis según la cual estos animales eran exclusivamente carnívoros se ha desacreditado, y todos los estudios recientes favorecen una forma de vida herbívora u omnívora para estos animales

facts.statement: Paul Barrett proposed that prosauropods supplemented their herbivorous diets with small prey or carrion.
facts.quote: Paul Barrett propuso que los prosaurópodos complementaban sus dietas herbívoras con presas pequeñas o carroña

facts.statement: No Plateosaurus fossils have been found with gastroliths (stomach stones) in the stomach area.
facts.quote: No se han encontrado fósiles de Plateosaurus con gastrolitos (piedras estomacales) en el área del estómago

facts.statement: Plateosaurus followed a growth trajectory similar to sauropods but with variable growth rates and final sizes like modern reptiles, likely due to environmental factors such as food availability.
facts.quote: Plateosaurus seguía una trayectoria de crecimiento parecida a la de los saurópodos, pero con una tasa de crecimiento y un tamaño final variables como en los reptiles actuales probablemente en respuesta a factores ambientales que podían afectar, por ejemplo, a la disponibilidad de comida

facts.statement: Some individuals reached full development at only 4.8 meters in length, while others grew to 10 meters.
facts.quote: Algunos individuos alcanzaron su desarrollo total con solo 4.8 metros de longitud, mientras que otros alcanzaban los 10 metros

facts.statement: Bone microstructure indicates rapid growth similar to sauropods and extinct mammals, suggesting endothermy.
facts.quote: No obstante, la microestructura ósea indica un crecimiento rápido, como en los saurópodos y los mamíferos extintos, lo cual sugiere endotermia

facts.statement: Studies by Sander and Klein found some individuals fully developed at 12 years, others growing slowly at 20 years, and one still in rapid growth at 18 years.
facts.quote: Sander y Klein hallaron que algunos individuos estaban completamente desarrollados a los 12 años de edad, otros aún estaban creciendo lentamente a los 20 años, y un individuo aún estaba en la etapa rápida de crecimiento a los 18 años

facts.statement: The oldest individual found was 27 years old and still growing.
facts.quote: El individuo más viejo encontrado tenía 27 años y seguía creciendo

facts.statement: The genus Plateosaurus was named by Meyer in 1837.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Plateosaurus (genus), Meyer 1837

facts.statement: Plateosaurus belongs to the parent group Plateosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Plateosauridae

facts.statement: The family of Plateosaurus is Plateosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Plateosauridae

facts.statement: Plateosaurus is classified in the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Plateosaurus lived from the Norian to the Hettangian stages, between 227.3 and 199.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Hettangian (227.3 to 199.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 36 recorded fossil occurrences of Plateosaurus in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 36
